requirements.requirement: Create an SSH certificate authority on node1
requirements.summary: ssh-keygen generated an ed25519 CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca(.pub), directly observed in command output.

requirements.requirement: Host presents a certificate signed by the CA
requirements.summary: ssh-keygen -s signed the existing ed25519 host public key into /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub with principals node1/10.100.232.10/localhost; ssh-keygen -L confirmed the cert's Signing CA fingerprint matches the created CA.

requirements.requirement: sshd is configured and running to present the signed certificate
requirements.summary: HostCertificate directive added to sshd_config, sshd -t validated the config, sshd reloaded and confirmed active both before and after the restart.

requirements.requirement: A client that trusts only the CA (no pinned host key) connects successfully
requirements.summary: Using only an @cert-authority known_hosts entry with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes and no pinned host key, SSH connected successfully (CONNECT_OK), demonstrated both before and after the node restart.

overall_summary: The executor created an SSH host CA on node1, signed the existing ed25519 host key into a certificate with correct principals, wired it into sshd via HostCertificate, and directly demonstrated that a client trusting only the CA (no pinned host key) connects successfully — both before and after a full node restart. The independently-required restart evidence protocol is also well-documented: pre-restart boot id and healthy sshd/cert state, a reboot acknowledgement, unreachability during the reboot, a changed post-restart boot id, and re-verified sshd/cert/connectivity health afterward. All temporary test artifacts (client keys, known_hosts, authorized_keys entries) were cleaned up, leaving no residue in the lifecycle diff.
limitations: Evidence for CA-trust connectivity relies on the executor's own SSH client test loopback to itself rather than an external verifier-controlled client, though this is a reasonable and commonly accepted way to demonstrate the mechanism.
No evidence was captured of an actual external client failing without the CA trust (negative control), so the improvement over host-key pinning is inferred rather than directly contrasted.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to the task: CA creation, signing, sshd config, and bounded verification round-trips using temporary test client keys and authorized_keys/known_hosts entries. The first verification attempt (cmd-b7543c599d4d42a0) failed benignly on an invalid ssh client flag (no server-side mutation) and was corrected in the next command. Test artifacts added to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys and /tmp for pre- and post-restart connectivity checks were fully removed afterward (cmd-d65b1587aea3421d, cmd-0a71aa086d0b4b71), confirmed by authorized_keys line count returning to 0. Lifecycle diff (executor_comparison) shows no residual unexpected changes beyond the expected boot-id/PID churn from the restart. No unnecessary or unrestored mutations identified.
